title: Matoi: Selective Revalidation of Consequence Evidence for Agent Authorization
text: arXiv:2610.21394 [ pdf , ps , other ] cs.CR cs.AI Matoi: Selective Revalidation of Consequence Evidence for Agent Authorization Authors: Zexun Wang Abstract : …10.87 and 16.53 percent; five of twelve family intervals for the matched comparison cross one in each language. A prospectively frozen AgentDojo Banking mapping covers 5/16 user plans and 7/9 attack… ▽ More Matoi separates reusable consequence evidence from current execution authority and durable occurrence history. Its finite query-aware contract covers branches, ordered collections and negative lookups. A consumer reuses only its own checked evidence whose observations remain valid; signed requests, live grants, quota and uncertain outcomes remain separate obligations. Conditional correctness arguments distinguish locally serialized claims from nontransactional remote effects. Two studies strengthen cost attribution and domain evaluation. A 1,440-cell matched-wire study repeats 144 authored inputs. With compact input bytes identical, reuse reduces complete lifecycle cost by 3.49 percent in JS and 1.79 percent in Python. Combined representation/reuse reductions against full proof are 10.87 and 16.53 percent; five of twelve family intervals for the matched comparison cross one in each language. A prospectively frozen AgentDojo Banking mapping covers 5/16 user plans and 7/9 attack plans . Both governed strategies preserve five exact benign transfers and refuse 35 reused attack- plan /policy crosses. Pre-satisfied utility predicates are reported separately from completed work. These are original scripted synthetic tools, not autonomous agents or a real bank. Earlier studies retain cheaper protected-cache alternatives, policy-compatible phishing, provider duplication and post-claim revocation . Separate JS/Python consumers establish finite-profile interoperability within the same project; durable recovery rechecks evidence and retains uncertain reservations. The results support a bounded, auditable reuse and execution contract, not a new general incremental algorithm, arbitrary-tool closure, atomic third-party commitment or production superiority. △ Less Submitted 15 October, 2026; originally announced October 2026. Comments: 55 pages, 4 figures. Includes an 18-page technical manuscript and a 33-page detailed supplement as ancillary files. Research preprint; not peer reviewed

title: Clawed and Dangerous: Can We Trust Open Agentic Systems?
text:
arXiv:2603.26221 [ pdf , ps , other ] cs.CR cs.AI cs.ET cs.SE Clawed and Dangerous: Can We Trust Open Agentic Systems? Authors: Shiping Chen , Qin Wang , Guangsheng Yu , Xu Wang , Liming Zhu Abstract : Open agentic systems combine LLM-based… ▽ More Open agentic systems combine LLM-based planning with external capabilities, persistent memory, and privileged execution. They are used in coding assistants, browser copilots, and enterprise automation. OpenClaw is a visible instance of this broader class.
  Without much attention yet, their security challenge is fundamentally different from that of traditional software that relies on predictable execution and well-defined control flow. In open agentic systems, everything is ''probabilistic'': plans are generated at runtime, key decisions may be shaped by untrusted natural-language inputs and tool outputs, execution unfolds in uncertain environments, and actions are taken under authority delegated by human users. The central challenge is therefore not merely robustness against individual attacks, but the governance of agentic behavior under persistent uncertainty.
  This paper systematizes the area through a software engineering lens. We introduce a six-dimensional analytical taxonomy and synthesize 50 papers spanning attacks, benchmarks, defenses, audits, and adjacent engineering foundations. From this synthesis, we derive a reference doctrine for secure-by-construction agent platforms, together with an evaluation scorecard for assessing platform security posture. Our review shows that the literature is relatively mature in attack characterization and benchmark construction, but remains weak in deployment controls, operational governance, persistent-memory integrity, and capability revocation . These gaps define a concrete engineering agenda for building agent ecosystems that are governable, auditable, and resilient under compromise. △ Less Submitted 27 March, 2026; originally announced March 2026.

title: Empower Healthcare through a Self-Sovereign Identity Infrastructure for Secure Electronic Health Data Access
text: arXiv:2501.12229 [ pdf , other ] cs.CR cs.DC Empower Healthcare through a Self-Sovereign Identity Infrastructure for Secure Electronic Health Data Access Authors: Antonio López Martínez , Montassar Naghmouchi , Maryline Laurent , Joaquin Garcia-Alfaro , Manuel Gil Pérez , Antonio Ruiz Martínez , Pantaleone Nespoli Abstract : …Decentralized Identifiers and Verifiable Credentials. The framework uses Blockchain technology to provide immutability, verifiable data registry, and auditability, as well as an agent -based model to provide protection and privacy for the patient data. We also define different use cases regarding the daily patient-practitioner-laboratory interactions and spec… ▽ More Health data is one of the most sensitive data for people, which attracts the attention of malicious activities. We propose an open-source health data management framework, that follows a patient-centric approach. The proposed framework implements the Self-Sovereign Identity paradigm with innovative technologies such as Decentralized Identifiers and Verifiable Credentials. The framework uses Blockchain technology to provide immutability, verifiable data registry, and auditability, as well as an agent -based model to provide protection and privacy for the patient data. We also define different use cases regarding the daily patient-practitioner-laboratory interactions and specific functions to cover patient data loss, data access revocation , and emergency cases where patients are unable to give consent and access to their data. To address this design, a proof of concept is created with an interaction between patient and doctor. The most feasible technologies are selected and the created design is validated. We discuss the differences and novelties of this framework, which includes the patient-centric approach also for data storage, the designed recovery and emergency plan , the defined backup procedure, and the selected blockchain platform. △ Less Submitted 21 January, 2025; originally announced January 2025. Comments: 40 pages, 11 figures
